rightsNote:
Everything in this knowledge base is written by icanspeak Portuguese and generated from this site's own data. None of it is scanned, copied or taken in part from a coursebook — that is exactly why we can give it away. Every file says at the bottom where it comes from.

What is deliberately NOT here: audio and book files from publishers and exam bodies (coursebooks, CAPLE or Celpe-Bras preparation books). We are not allowed to pass those on, not even for free and not even in class. Instead, we link to the official pages of the exam bodies and dictionaries — see “Official materials”. icanspeak Portuguese is not affiliated with CAPLE, the University of Lisbon or the Camões institute.

files.title: Portuguese Grammar Start A1–B1 – The 10 most important chapters
files.desc: The starter book: the ten most important grammar chapters for everyday life and exams, with rules, tables, exercises and answers, explained in simple English.

files.title: Grammar A1–B2 (complete)
files.desc: Every grammar topic from A1 to B2 in one volume, with a table of contents, rules, example sentences and all the summary tables.

files.title: Grammar A1
files.desc: Gender and articles with their contractions (do, na, ao), ser and estar, the present tense, questions, plurals, gostar de, telling the time and more.

files.title: Grammar A2
files.desc: Perfeito simples and imperfeito, ir + infinitive, estar a + infinitive, object pronouns after the verb, comparatives, a, para or em and more.

files.title: Grammar B1
files.desc: Perfeito composto or simples, future and conditional, the imperative, the present and future subjunctive, por or para, relative clauses, where the pronoun goes and more.

files.title: Grammar B2
files.desc: The imperfect subjunctive, unreal conditions, passive and se, reported speech, the personal infinitive, verbs of change, collocations and more.

files.desc: About 1,800 words from A1 to B2 in one volume, ordered by level and 160 learning sets — with o or a, plural, an English meaning and an example sentence.

links.title: CAPLE: Portuguese as a foreign language exams
links.note: The official information on the CAPLE exams (ACESSO, CIPLE, DEPLE, DIPLE, DAPLE, DUPLE): levels, dates, centres and sample material. We don't copy it — there it is always up to date.

links.title: Camões, I.P.
links.source: Camões – Instituto da Cooperação e da Língua
links.note: Portugal's institute for the Portuguese language abroad: courses, language centres and information on the language.

links.title: Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa
links.note: A free online dictionary that shows the Portugal spelling next to the Brazilian one, with meanings and every verb's conjugation.

links.title: Ciberdúvidas da Língua Portuguesa
links.source: Ciberdúvidas, ISCTE – Instituto Universitário de Lisboa

links.title: AIMA: Agência para a Integração, Migrações e Asilo
links.note: The official source for residence permits in Portugal. Rules and procedures change often: always check here, not on this site.

links.title: Infopédia: dictionaries of Porto Editora
links.note: Portuguese dictionaries and bilingual dictionaries (English–Portuguese and more), in the Portugal standard.

links.title: Portal das Finanças
links.note: The tax authority: the NIF, the annual tax return (IRS) and the letters you get from Finanças. The official texts are in Portuguese, a good real-life reading exercise.

links.title: Segurança Social
links.note: Social security in Portugal: the NISS number, contributions and benefits. Check the current rules there, not on this site.

links.title: ePortugal: the public services portal
links.note: The government's guide to public services, from the número de utente to the Cartão de Cidadão. Many pages exist in English too.

links.title: IMT: Instituto da Mobilidade e dos Transportes
links.note: The official source for the Portuguese driving licence, exchanging a foreign licence and the theory exam.
